title: Claude Fable 5.2 vs Opus 5.5: 10 Real Builds (Opus Still Wins!!)
brief:
Today's video is modelled on the YouTube video "Claude Fable 5.2 vs Opus 5.5: 10 Real Builds (Opus Still Wins!!)" by Outskill (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LfJfCJdpeog), chosen by the owner. Explain the same subject: what happened, how it works and what the viewer can do with it. Gather the facts from other credible sources, not only that video.
What that video says (for the subject only, never its sentences): For most of this year, Anthropic has been building something they wouldn't let the public touch. A model powerful enough that they only handed it to vetted cyber security labs and life science research groups cleared through US government programs. No consumer plan, no API, not even their biggest customers got access. They called that model mythos. A few months ago, they built a public version of it. Same brain, extra safeguards wrapped around it and quietly shipped it to paid claude users. That one is called Fable. It sits in a new fourth tier above Opus, above everything most of us have been using for serious work. This Monday, Anthropic released the newest version of that public model, Fable 5.2. And before they let anyone near it, they gave it a test. They handed it two unsolved problems from the physics of black holes, the kind actual physicists have been staring at for years. It solved both. That's the kind of model Fable 5.2 is. And here's what that actually means for you. It beats Opus 5.5, the model you've probably been using for the hard stuff on almost everything that matters, coding, reasoning, computer use, research. On top of that, it runs 30% faster than the last Fable and costs 20% less to use. 55% fewer blocks, too, which is a polite way of saying it finally stops refusing things it shouldn't have been refusing in the first place. But the real unlock, the thing most of the launch coverage missed, is what it does when you point it at a long, messy job. You know the kind the task that used to take three prompts, a lot of handholding, and still came back half wrong. Fable does it in one pass. You give it the brief, you walk away, and it comes back when the work is done. That's the gap it closes. That's what's new.
